South Elizabeth Seychelles Hospital INTERNAL MEDICINE DEPARTMENT Location: 4923 Olivia Parkway Suite 217, Lake Jennabury
PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 78 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 02/14/26 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit for COPD management, evaluation of persistent bilateral lower extremity edema, and assessment of worsening fatigue and psychological well-being.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax returns for a follow-up visit, with ongoing concerns regarding his chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), persistent bilateral lower extremity edema, and worsening fatigue. Since his last visit, he reports that the daytime dyspnea has slightly improved with the increased use of the albuterol inhaler, which he now utilizes approximately six times a day. However, he still experiences significant shortness of breath with minimal exertion, particularly during cold weather.
The bilateral lower extremity edema remains unchanged despite adherence to dietary sodium restrictions and continued furosemide therapy at 80 mg daily. The edema is still noted as 1+ pitting, particularly after prolonged sitting, and Mr. Fairfax reports no associated pain or redness. He expresses frustration regarding the lack of improvement and its impact on his mobility.
His fatigue continues to be debilitating, and he describes it as worsening to the point that it limits his ability to engage in social activities and perform daily tasks. Mr. Fairfax also reports increased feelings of anxiety and sadness, indicating that he has been experiencing more frequent episodes of depressed mood, likely secondary to his chronic health issues.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + worsening fatigue, no fevers or chills. Pulmonary - + daytime dyspnea, + nocturnal wheezing, - cough, - sputum production, no hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain or palpitations, + orthopnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - + joint pain in knees and hands, no swelling. Neurological - no dizziness or headaches.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) 2. Hypertension 3. Osteoarthritis 4. Persistent fatigue 5. Anxiety and depression (new diagnosis)
PAST SURGICAL HISTORY
1. Right knee arthroscopy in 2018.
FAMILY HISTORY
Father - history of lung cancer. Mother - history of hypertension.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives alone in , . Former carpenter, now retired. Quit smoking 15 years ago. Occasional alcohol use. No illicit drug use.
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
MEDICATIONS ON FOLLOW-UP
1. Albuterol inhaler as needed, increased use to six times daily. 2. Lisinopril 20 mg daily. 3. Fluticasone/salmeterol 500/50 MDI, 1 puff twice daily. 4. Tiotropium 18 mcg inhaler, 1 puff daily. 5. Acetaminophen 500 mg as needed for pain. 6. Furosemide 80 mg daily. 7. Sertraline 50 mg daily (newly initiated for anxiety and depression).
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: T 98.6F, HR 78, BP 126/80, RR 22, O2 sat 89% on room air
General: Elderly male in no acute distress but appears fatigued and anxious. HEENT: No nasal congestion, oropharynx clear. Pulmonary: Diminished breath sounds bilaterally, moderate wheezing noted on expiration, no crackles. Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs. Extremities: 1+ pitting edema in bilateral lower extremities, no erythema or warmth.
LABORATORY DATA
1. CBC: WBC 8.7, Hgb 11.8, Hct 34.8, Plt 215 2. BMP: Na 136, K 4.0, Cl 94, CO2 26, BUN 19, Cr 1.2, Glucose 88 3. BNP: 490 (stable). 4. Thyroid function tests: TSH 3.4 (within normal limits).
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. COPD management: Despite some improvement in daytime symptoms with increased albuterol use, the patient continues to experience significant dyspnea. Maintain the current regimen of tiotropium and fluticasone/salmeterol. Discussed the potential for a referral to pulmonary rehabilitation to enhance exercise tolerance and quality of life. Follow-up in 1 month for reassessment. 2. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril. Blood pressure remains stable. Follow-up in 1 month. 3. Lower extremity edema: The edema persists. Reinforce dietary sodium restrictions and encourage Mr. Fairfax to elevate his legs more frequently. Referral to nephrology will be arranged if no improvement is noted by the next follow-up. 4. Fatigue and psychological well-being: Given the worsening fatigue and new diagnosis of anxiety and depression, continue sertraline 50 mg daily. Schedule follow-up with a psychologist for ongoing support. Monitor CBC and metabolic panel in one month to assess for any changes.
Patient education reiterated regarding recognizing signs of exacerbation, adherence to medication, and lifestyle modifications to effectively manage COPD and edema.
